tile_identity.instances: A tile holds one instance per subtopic. Core1A: one construction per instance. Core1B: one MAIN cycle whose attempt mixes instances and carries the tile band, plus one cycle per instance (same coverage as Core1A). Instance cycles may score below the tile band; their real level is labelled.

exam_question.role: Core2 custody: the real exam question this tile prepares her for.
exam_question.show: Exact text, options and figure as published, with its source line (exam, date, shift). No answer, no hint, no level label.
exam_question.rule: If the tile has no real exam question at its band, say so on the page ('no exam question yet') rather than inventing one.

core1a.role: Teaching part: the full reasoning, completed and visible.

sections.title: Conventions
sections.rule: Axes, signs, frame, system and reference levels the topic adapter declares, stated before use.

sections.title: Before you start
sections.rule: Prerequisite bridge: each entry assumption from the adapter, with a compact explanation or a link to where it is taught.

sections.title: Build the idea
sections.rule: Ordered steps; each step = action + why it is valid + the picture stage it uses + source ref. Column shape in columns.*.core1a_build.

sections.title: Worked anchor
sections.rule: A completed example at the tile's band, DIFFERENT from the exam question, reasoning shown in full including steps an expert would skip, ending with a check.

sections.title: A plausible wrong path
sections.rule: The column's wrong idea in this topic's words, a diagnostic question that exposes it, and the repair.

sections.title: Close the idea
sections.rule: Exit task with its full answer and a check she can run alone.

core1b.role: Her try: she performs the same inference before it is revealed, then checks and repairs without a tutor.
core1b.cycles: Main cycle first (band-carrying, mixes instances), then one cycle per instance. Each cycle runs the six sections below.

sections.title: 1 · Predict
sections.rule: One decision she can commit to before anything is revealed; closes with a defensible answer.

sections.title: 2 · Construct your response
sections.rule: A fresh task (not Core1A with nouns changed). States what she must produce. Its band is checked by common.band_check. Her first answer is saved before any help.

sections.title: 3 · Compare and reconstruct
sections.rule: The correct construction reached the way a learner would reach it; rubric, accepted reasoning, rejected reasoning and why.

sections.title: 4 · Diagnose
sections.rule: The plausible wrong answer named, with a question that separates it from the right one; records MISCONCEPTION only from her saved answer.

sections.title: 5 · Repair
sections.rule: What she changes or rebuilds, linked to the exact Core1A step.

sections.title: 6 · Edge case
sections.rule: A limiting, reversed or exception case that confirms understanding rather than recall; closed.

return_to_exam_question.rule: After Core1B she answers the exam question shown at the start. Only then are its answer, solution and source key shown. If the exam question's level is below the tile's band, it is labelled with its real level.

source_view.rule: Hidden by default: sources, exam custody (URL, paper, key status), band_check scores, blueprint/adapter versions, gap notes.

rules: Before her attempt is saved: givens-only pictures; hints H1-H3 only; no verdict, model name, bridge or warrant that is her protected work.
Core1A of the same tile may teach the idea, but its worked anchor must not be the Core1B task or the exam question.
The exam question's answer is shown only after she answers it.

H1.rule: Help her state exactly what the question turns on.

H2.rule: Link that crux to something she has already shown she can do (Y).

H3.rule: Open the route (Z) without doing the protected step (W).

hint_ladder.never: No hint contains W, the answer, or eliminates options for her.

picture_rules.S1: Shows the situation and makes the crux legible, without the answer.
picture_rules.S2: Connects what she already holds to this situation.
picture_rules.S3: Supports construction toward the crux without completing it.
picture_rules.meaning_check: Every stage is bound to a named reasoning step. The drawn bodies, arrows, labels and values must match that step's scene; a familiar fallback picture is a failure. A picture that only decorates is replaced by a justified 'no picture' note.
picture_rules.accessibility: Each stage has a text description; labels at least 14 px.

review_objectives.source: Shared/quality/question-demand-templates.v1.json -> templates[template_ref].review (questions resolved per cell in the resolved file)
review_objectives.P1: PROTECT: pre-attempt panels orient without handing over her decisive work
review_objectives.P2: ROUTE: concept links reach the exact bridge or repair she needs
review_objectives.P3: EXPLAIN_AND_CHECK: post-attempt reasoning explains validity and verifies independently
review_objectives.M1: DIAGNOSE: the likely wrong route is represented
review_objectives.M2: DETECT: separates a held misconception from a one-off slip
review_objectives.M3: REPAIR: makes the failure visible and establishes the replacement rule
review_objectives.naming_note: These review codes P1-P3 are not the learner's first assessment (also called P1 in the Owner's workflow).

evidence_record.first_answer: Saved, with time, before any hint, reveal or Core1A link is opened from the attempt.
evidence_record.help_exposure: Each hint or reveal opened, in order.
evidence_record.revisions: Kept separately from the first answer.
evidence_record.rule: Helped work is never DEMONSTRATED. A correct result without the column's evidence criterion is UNCERTAIN. No mastery claims.

band_check.applies_to: Every Core1B attempt task and every exam question placed in the tile, each scored separately.
band_check.scoring_rule: Score the learner-owned work the exact task requires before support, using the rubric anchors in learner-question-metadata.v1.json; one evidence sentence per component; never score one difficulty twice.
band_check.primary_demand_rule: Exactly one primary demand: the act whose success most directly decides the task. If scoring pushes the decisive act into another column (see columns.*.boundary), move the task to that column.
band_check.lower_level_material: Exam questions scoring below the tile band may appear only as labelled bridge examples in Core1A or as the exam question with its real level shown; they never count as coverage at the tile band.
band_check.independence: Author's score is PROPOSED until someone other than the author scores it.

self_audit_before_render.format: Each check: result PASS/FAIL/NOT_APPLICABLE + specific evidence + reason when NOT_APPLICABLE. A FAIL blocks rendering.

common.closure: Every prompt in Core1A and Core1B closes with a model response, a rubric, or accepted/rejected answers. Nothing is deferred to a teacher.

invariants: Academic truth comes from the topic adapter's canonical refs (subject library); exam questions and learner observations supply demand evidence, never replacement truth.

column.her_move: Pick or reconstruct the right fact, category, definition, unit, sign or condition, deciding by its defining condition.

slots.Y: a demonstrated anchor that lets her rebuild the fact instead of guessing
slots.Z: classify using the defining condition

pictures.job: Make the deciding feature visible; otherwise a justified 'no picture'.

column.boundary: If executing a relation decides it -> Apply. If choosing a governing law to solve decides it -> Model. If reading a graph/diagram decides it -> Represent.
adapter_slots_required: subtopics[].facts[]: fact, deciding_condition, holds_when, fails_when, near_neighbour, trap_cases[], quick_check, misconception_refs[], picture

core1b_shape.attempt: Classify a fresh set of cases; for each, verdict + deciding condition.
core1b_shape.boundary_test: A case where the condition flips the familiar verdict.

column.evidence_criterion: DEMONSTRATED only when each verdict comes with its correct deciding condition. Right verdict without the condition = UNCERTAIN.

cell.attempt_pattern: Main cycle: classify at least 4 fresh cases drawn from at least 2 subtopics, including one near-neighbour pair and one exception; verdict + deciding condition for each; at least one case reaches its condition in two dependent steps.

cell.support_may_show: The candidate categories and the definitions' wording; never which case goes where.

column.core1a_build: Claim -> warrant -> conditions -> proof -> where the claim fails.

core1b_shape.attempt: Prove or refute a fresh claim, stating warrant and conditions.
core1b_shape.boundary_test: The converse, or the claim with one condition removed.

column.evidence_criterion: DEMONSTRATED when warrant and conditions are explicit, the chain is valid, and the boundary case is handled.

cell.attempt_pattern: A claim whose converse or boundary case is false, or a derivation in a new context; she must state where it fails.
cell.protected: The warrant and the failing condition.

main_template.decisive_act: Establish a conclusion from explicit warrants or evidence.

slots.X: the claim to establish and the evidence or conditions that may legitimately support it
slots.Y: a demonstrated theorem, principle, data rule, or warrant
slots.Z: construct a valid claim-to-warrant-to-conclusion argument
slots.W: the decisive warrant, inference, or proof step that establishes the claim. Band protection: Leave the decisive model, strategy, synthesis, exception, or warrant itself to the learner; support may clarify constraints and invariants only.
slots.wrong_idea: an example, diagram, pattern, authority statement, or numerical coincidence is treated as proof
slots.replacement_rule: state the warrant explicitly and show why its conditions license this conclusion
slots.visual_job: show givens, evidence, and construction relationships without marking the conclusion as established
slots.check_job: challenge the argument with a counterexample, converse, boundary case, independent derivation, or evidence-consistency test

band_policy.protected_work: Leave the decisive model, strategy, synthesis, exception, or warrant itself to the learner; support may clarify constraints and invariants only.
band_policy.support_posture: Preserve the decisive abstraction or strategy choice even when additional optional support is available later.

H1.objective: The learner can state what the question turns on before choosing a route.
H1.question: Can hint 1 help this learner clarify the claim to establish and the evidence or conditions that may legitimately support it?

H2.objective: The learner connects the crux to knowledge already held.
H2.question: Can hint 2 help this learner correlate the claim to establish and the evidence or conditions that may legitimately support it with a demonstrated theorem, principle, data rule, or warrant, and see why that bridge applies here?

H3.objective: The learner can start the crux without being handed the protected work.
H3.question: Can hint 3 open the way to construct a valid claim-to-warrant-to-conclusion argument while leaving the decisive warrant, inference, or proof step that establishes the claim to the learner? Leave the decisive model, strategy, synthesis, exception, or warrant itself to the learner; support may clarify constraints and invariants only.

S1.objective: The first visual stage makes the situation and crux legible without answering it.
S1.question: Does stage 1 show the situation and help this learner see the claim to establish and the evidence or conditions that may legitimately support it, without disclosing the decisive warrant, inference, or proof step that establishes the claim?

S2.objective: A visual stage connects the learner's held idea to this question.
S2.question: Does a stage show a demonstrated theorem, principle, data rule, or warrant in this question's context? Visual job: show givens, evidence, and construction relationships without marking the conclusion as established.

S3.objective: A later visual stage supports construction toward the crux without completing it.
S3.question: Does a later stage show the way toward construct a valid claim-to-warrant-to-conclusion argument while leaving the decisive warrant, inference, or proof step that establishes the claim to the learner?

P1.objective: Pre-attempt panels orient without handing over the decisive learner work.
P1.question: Do all pre-attempt panels leave the decisive warrant, inference, or proof step that establishes the claim to the learner? Leave the decisive model, strategy, synthesis, exception, or warrant itself to the learner; support may clarify constraints and invariants only.

P2.objective: Concept navigation reaches the exact bridge or repair the learner needs.
P2.question: Does the concept link land where the bridge from the claim to establish and the evidence or conditions that may legitimately support it to a demonstrated theorem, principle, data rule, or warrant is actually taught or repaired?

P3.objective: Post-attempt reasoning explains validity and verifies independently.
P3.question: Does each solution move explain why it holds here, and does the check challenge the argument with a counterexample, converse, boundary case, independent derivation, or evidence-consistency test?

M1.objective: The likely conceptual wrong route is explicitly represented.
M1.question: Is this likely wrong idea represented: an example, diagram, pattern, authority statement, or numerical coincidence is treated as proof?

M2.objective: The diagnostic distinguishes a held misconception from a one-off execution slip.
M2.question: Would a learner who holds 'an example, diagram, pattern, authority statement, or numerical coincidence is treated as proof' answer the diagnostic differently from a learner who merely slipped?

M3.objective: The repair makes the failure visible and establishes a replacement rule.
M3.question: Does the repair show why 'an example, diagram, pattern, authority statement, or numerical coincidence is treated as proof' fails and establish this replacement rule: state the warrant explicitly and show why its conditions license this conclusion?
